message.content: {"mechanism_id":"cr-memory-antithetic-reweighting","target_component":"M_CR weighted arithmetic mean update in L-SHADE memory","observed_evidence":{"task_id":"TASK-02","trace_path":"diagnostic_trace_summary","function":"F10","seed":0,"metric":"CR_mean_drift","observed_value":0.98},"causal_hypothesis":"Successful trials with CR near current M_CR get large |delta_f| weights, so the weighted mean reinforces its own center, creating positive feedback that drives M_CR to extremes.","algorithmic_change":"Replace the single weighted arithmetic mean with an antithetic reweighting: split successful trials into those above and below current M_CR, compute each subgroup's weighted mean, and set M_CR to their average weighted by subgroup success mass, pulling the estimate toward the population's CR centroid.","mathematical_rule":"Let S = successful trials, w_j = |delta_f_j|. Split S_hi = {j: CR_j >= M_CR}, S_lo = {j: CR_j < M_CR}. m_hi = sum(w_j*CR_j, j in S_hi)/sum(w_j, j in S_hi), m_lo similarly. M_CR_new = (W_hi*m_hi + W_lo*m_lo)/(W_hi + W_lo) where W_hi = sum(w_j, j in S_hi), W_lo = sum(w_j, j in S_lo). If one side empty, keep standard update.","expected_effect":"Dampens runaway drift by forcing M_CR to reflect both sides of its current value, keeping F1/F6/F10 CR_mean in 0.4-0.7 and preventing F20 collapse to 0.02.","failure_prediction":"On unimodal separable functions where high CR is genuinely optimal, antithetic averaging may slow convergence by keeping M_CR near 0.5 too long.","ablation_plan":"Compare canonical weighted mean vs antithetic reweighting on 12 functions x 5 seeds; also test antithetic with W_hi,W_lo replaced by equal weights to isolate the mass-weighting contribution.","nearest_known_methods":"Adaptive CR memory in L-SHADE, weighted Lehmer/arithmetic memory updates, antithetic sampling in evolution strategies.","implementation_requirements":"Track per-success CR_j and delta_f_j within each generation; compute subgroup sums before memory update; handle empty subgroups by falling back to standard weighted mean; no extra memory beyond two accumulators."}
